title: SmartHow Workspace Agent
lead: Cut writing a new technical document from 3 hours to 10 minutes.
description: Agentic chat that writes and edits long-form technical documents. Designed and built the agent loop from scratch, chosen over LangGraph and Temporal: parallel tool calls, cross-turn memory, pause/resume and a stop policy with a cost cap. Moved tools to a per-tool registry, replaced the blind spinner with a live activity stream over WebSockets, reached ~76% prompt-cache reads with a per-session HMAC delimiter, and added voice dictation through Whisper.

title: Document Asset Ingestion
lead: Zero cross-document leakage in the isolation eval.
description: Retrieval layer that turns uploaded PDFs and audio transcripts into dependable context for the writing agent. Parsing, chunking and full-text search over Postgres, assets scoped per document with per-library permissions, and binary storage on an RBAC-only Azure Blob port with no public URLs.

title: Monorepo CI/CD Hardening
lead: CI tests from 44 to 254, high advisories from 10 to 0.
description: Audited and rebuilt delivery for a multi-app monorepo. Restored the Azure OIDC federation that had silently broken every deploy, rebuilt the dev deploy as blue-green, made quality gates required on protected branches, and added CodeQL, dependency audits, SHA-pinned actions and mutation testing.

title: Azure Cost Program
lead: About US$1k a month saved across 127 cloud resources.
description: Cloud cost initiative over 17 resource groups (US$0.9–1.07k/month at list price): mapped the full spend, decommissioned the staging environment and a superseded production stack, purged and downgraded container registries, right-sized app plans, and rerouted expensive model traffic to cheaper deployments.

title: Rashomon
lead: Which words stick to 27 Brazilian public figures.
description: Collects what Bluesky, Google News, GDELT, the press and both houses of Congress say about 27 Brazilian public figures, then draws the words that keep landing next to each name: how often, how surprising, from which outlet and in what tone. Every number opens to the texts behind it.
how: Collect: each source has its own collector with the same signature, storing text, URL, outlet, date and tone.
Extract: the text is normalized into hashtags, words and phrases. A document that names nobody tracked is dropped, not stored.
Score: terms are counted per person and scored with PMI against every document that mentions anyone tracked.
Serve: a Hono API, and a SvelteKit front end prerendered at build time.
notes: Frequency and PMI answer different questions. The map sorts by PMI times ln(1 + count), so a word seen twice cannot outrank one seen two hundred times.
Tone comes only from GDELT. Every other source stores no tone rather than an invented one.

Tone toward each person comes from kikori, a separate model, and the page says plainly that it carries a name prior: read it as one outlet against others on the same person, never as person against person.
An outlet's political lean is a judgment with citations, and a missing outlet means nobody has researched it, not that it is neutral.

title: Desafinado
lead: Every AI suggestion is a tracked change you can refuse.
description: Markdown editor with an AI co-author, for prose and for agent Skills. The name comes from Jobim's song in defense of the singer who is slightly out of tune: the AI proposes, your voice wins. Ships as an Electron app with a Skills library and evals, and as a web app.
how: Ask about a passage with Ctrl+K: a quick action or any instruction.
The answer lands in the text as a tracked change, old text struck through, with a one-line rationale on a card in the margin.
Accept, reject or refine it. Accept is an ordinary edit, so Ctrl+Z undoes it.
A review pass reads the whole document and streams up to six suggestions, and the timeline keeps a version after each step, marked by who made it.
notes: The model returns structured output and the app owns the anchors, so a suggestion always points at real text in the document.
Small edits show a word-level diff and rewrites show the whole block.
Only validated streams reach the text: a partial answer that fails the schema is never applied.
Skill files on disk are the source of truth. When an agent, another editor or git changes the open file, the editor reloads it and records an external version.
The Evals page runs a Skill's evals through the Claude CLI with and without the Skill, to show whether it helped. The default model was picked by a bake-off.

title: Chrono Digger
lead: Students question AI witnesses grounded in historical sources.
description: History sim where students question AI characters grounded in primary sources, each frozen at a moment in history. Students deduce what happened by putting the voices together, and keep an investigation diary as they go. It started on a Sarajevo street on 28 June 1914.
how: Each pair of student and character gets its own Durable Object, with the conversation history and a hibernatable WebSocket.
A turn is one Effect: retrieve passages, build the prompt, stream the answer, attach its sources, all under one 45-second deadline.
Per-student and global daily quotas live in their own Durable Objects, and a failed turn is refunded.
Providers sit behind interfaces, so Workers AI and OpenRouter swap by configuration, and tests inject fakes at that seam.
notes: A fidelity eval with an LLM judge asked one question: is the free model faithful to its sources? It was not. It failed every round, at best 27 of 35, and the failures were not missing sources: the model got the right passage and skipped the sentence that mattered.
So the disputed questions now come from a written script reviewed by people, and the case can be closed with the script alone.
The model answers only free questions. Its answers are labeled as unchecked conversation, never enter the diary, and a disputed question asked freely is routed back to the script.
Infrastructure is code in Alchemy, and every pull request gets its own preview deployment, destroyed when it closes.

title: Cerberus
lead: A password manager that never leaves your machine.
description: Local-only TUI password manager with a single encrypted vault file. No server, no sync and no browser extension: the vault never leaves the machine, and what is on disk is useless without the master password.
how: The master password goes through Argon2id to make a wrapping key.
The wrapping key unwraps a random vault key, and only that vault key ever touches the entries.
The vault key opens the vault with XChaCha20-Poly1305, whose 24-byte nonce is safe to pick at random.
Saving writes a temp file and renames it over the vault, so a crash never leaves half a vault.
notes: Key material stays in byte slices that are zeroed by hand: a memguard LockedBuffer while in use, an Enclave at rest.
Every random byte comes from crypto/rand: passwords (20 characters by default) and diceware passphrases (6 words).
Copying a password starts a 30-second timer that clears the clipboard, on Wayland or X11.
Domain types never import crypto or file IO, so the vault model is tested on its own.

title: Anamnesis
lead: Answers job applications without your data leaving the browser.
description: Chromium side panel that answers job application questions from your own story bank of Markdown files. Semantic search with EmbeddingGemma and an optional WebLLM rewrite both run in the browser, so nothing about you leaves the machine, and it never submits a form.
specs: EmbeddingGemma 300M in a worker, vectors cached in IndexedDB

title: Mr. Argus
lead: A live dashboard of every Claude Code process.
description: Process monitor and analytics for Claude Code on Linux, read straight from /proc. A daemon tracks each instance and its token use, a terminal UI shows live process trees with CPU and memory sparklines, and a web dashboard charts cost, models, tools and cache efficiency.

title: Estante
lead: A shared shelf of music for a study group.
description: Shared shelf of album and track recommendations for a psychoacoustics study group. Installs as a share target, so a link sent on WhatsApp lands on the shelf with the form filled in, and filters live in the URL so any view can be shared.

title: Aetheria
lead: Ear training you play instead of answer.
description: Top-down action RPG where sound is world information: doors sing intervals, bells answer them, and enemies telegraph attacks by singing. The answer is always spatial (move, dodge, strike), never naming the interval. No engine, just canvas and Web Audio, with sounds synthesized at runtime on random roots so the player learns intervals, not pitches.

title: Homer
lead: Turns new commits into a written chronicle.
description: Git chronicle TUI, third sibling to Mr. Argus and Arachne. Watches a repository, groups new commits into narrative units (bursts, singles, merges) and writes them as prose through a pluggable narrator, either an LLM over OpenRouter or a template heuristic.

title: Arachne
lead: GitHub's Network tab, rebuilt for the terminal.
description: TUI git network graph viewer that replaces GitHub's Network tab. Renders commit DAGs with branch lanes, integrates with GitHub for fork/branch data, and live-reloads on new commits.

title: Smells Like Job Spirit
lead: A local LLM that helps with the job hunt.
description: Browser extension with Python backend and Ollama integration for job search assistance.

title: Apollo
lead: A review queue for new commits, in the terminal.
description: Local-first terminal app for commit review triage. Detects new commits in a local repository, notifies that they might need a review, tracks their status in SQLite and surfaces the unreviewed queue in a keyboard-first TUI.

title: AI Decco Assistant
description: Web app that takes a photo of an office and a request, such as a new wall color or a shelf with plants, and generates AI variations. Any variation can become the new base image for another round.

title: HTML to DOCX Converter
description: Python tool for converting HTML documents to DOCX format.

title: The Thought Weaver
description: TypeScript project for thought organization and note-taking.
